a1_subtitle: Sign in with your work email. We'll send you a one-time code.
a1_privacyReminder: Your wellbeing reports are not used for HR, pay, or promotion decisions. You can choose to report anonymously — when you do, your user ID is removed from the report before managers can see it.
a1_errRate: Too many requests. Try again in {n} minutes.
a1_errEmail: Please enter a valid email address.
a1_errNet: Couldn't reach the server. Check your connection.
a3_intro: We'd like a moment of your time. This is the agreement between you and the system — in plain language. Read it once; you can re-read it any time from Settings.
a3_whatBody: Your check-ins (an energy number 0–100) and any optional answers or comments you choose to add. Nothing else.
a3_useBody: Aggregated trends are shown to your ward manager. When a report is at the low or high extreme, an alert is created so a human can follow up.
a3_notUseBody: Not for HR processes. Not for pay or promotion decisions. Not for performance review. Not for disciplinary action.
a3_anonBody: Each report can be submitted anonymously. When you do, your user ID is removed server-side and replaced with a one-way token that cannot be reversed. Managers see only aggregate trends. Note: free text may identify you indirectly, and small groups may be hidden to protect privacy.
a3_erasureBody: Per Israeli Privacy Law Amendment 13, you can request deletion of your data at any time from Settings → Privacy. Anonymous reports cannot be tied back to you, so they are unaffected.
a3_check1: I understand that reports are used for identifying department-level trends only.
a3_check2: I understand I can report anonymously and my user ID is removed from the report.
a3_check3: I understand I can request data deletion at any time.
a3_declined: You can sign in again any time. Without consent, the system can't process your wellbeing reports.
b1_hint: Drag the battery up or down. Submit when it feels right.
b1_hint_battery: Drag the battery up or down. Submit when it feels right.
b1_hint_orb: Drag the slider left or right. Submit when it feels right.
b1_toggleHelpOn: Anonymous mode removes your user ID from the report before it appears on management dashboards. Managers see department-level patterns, not your identity.
b1_toggleHelpOff: Your name is attached to this report.
b3_q1: Did you feel supported by your manager this week?
b4_anonCaveat: This comment is anonymous — but if you describe a unique situation, your manager could potentially recognise you. Avoid identifying details if you want full anonymity.
b5_emptyUpdates: When your manager publishes updates based on the team's reports, they'll appear here.
f1_netErr: We can't reach our servers right now.
f1_netErrSub: Your data is safe. Nothing has been lost.
f2_authExpiredSub: For your privacy, sessions expire after a short period of inactivity. Sign in again to continue.
f2_whyBody: We never keep you logged in indefinitely. Your session is short by design to keep your reports private.
f3_notFoundSub: The link may have expired, or it was never valid. No data is missing — just this page.
offline: You're offline. Check-ins can't be submitted right now — try again when you're back online.
c1_emptyAlerts: No open alerts. Nothing requires immediate attention.
c1_nudgeUnderTitle: Your team is asking — and not hearing back
c1_nudgeUnderBody: {n} of your last {total} closures didn't become a team update. When closures stay private, the team has no signal that anything changed — and reporting drops over the next two weeks.
c1_nudgeOverTitle: Updates work best when they mean something
c1_nudgeOverBody: You've published {n} of your last {total} closures. When every closure becomes an update, the team starts to skim — and the loud signals get lost. Consider holding back the routine ones.
c1_nudgeThresholdNote: Heuristic: surfaces when ≥3 of the last 5 closures were unpublished, or ≥4 of 5 were published.
c1_nudgeZeroBody: {n} alerts opened this week, none closed. The longer alerts sit, the less the team trusts the system to do anything with their reports.
c1_nudgeDecayBody: Reporting dropped from {prev}% to {curr}% over the past two weeks. This usually means the team has stopped seeing the point. Recent unpublished closures are often why.
c8_title: Closures the team hasn't heard about
c8_subtitle: Closed alerts from the past 14 days that weren't shared as a team update. You can publish a short note now, or skip — it stays in your audit log either way.
c1_thresholdFootnote: Roles with fewer than {n} reports show no average — protecting individual privacy.
c1_emptyDashboard: Reports will appear here as your team starts checking in.
c2_closureHint: A short note for your own audit trail. Examples: "Spoke privately, scheduled follow-up", "Routed to social worker", "Team-wide intervention via Team Update".
c7_hint: Share what you've done in response to the team's reports. Plain language, no formatting.
c7_placeholder: This week we noticed energy was lower mid-shift on Wednesdays. Starting next week we're adding a 15-minute break rotation.
c7_published: Update published. Your team will see it on their next visit.
k1_body: 23 colleagues have already checked in today. You are not alone.
k2_body: 12 days of honest check-ins. Not always high. Not always low. Real.
k3_body: Someone on your team said thank you, anonymously, this week.
k4_body: 60 seconds to come back to yourself. Optional. Anytime.
k5_body: A private line for your eyes only. Never sent. Never read.
k6_body: A view across all hospitals in the Mehva network. Aggregated only.
k7_body: How are you, manager? Same battery. Same privacy. Different audience.
k8_body: When a colleague leaves, the team can write together. A single shared letter.
k9_body: A small note when something kind happened today. To remember.
k10_body: Good to know. The small institutional knowledge that should not get lost.
k11_body: Not a number. A colour you choose with your finger. Rich, ambiguous, real.
k12_body: Quarterly long-form check-in. Beyond the daily.
k13_body: No notifications during your protected times. The product respects sleep.
k14_body: Quiet, non-blaming language for when there is nothing to show.
k15_body: 20 seconds. Sometimes a voice says what a number can't.
